title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9-11): in the first draft of the 'Analysis situs' chapter (1986), Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, purely combinatorial framework for tame ('modérée') topology. A space is described by a set F_el of 'elementary figures' (model: closed tame pieces such as convex cells or closed strata) with two pieces of structure. (2) is a partial order ≤, meaning inclusion of figures. (3) is a reflexive symmetric relation R, 'compatible'. A configuration is a subset of F_el whose elements are pairwise compatible, i.e. a clique of the compatibility graph. Page 9 adds a distinguished class of 'locally finite' configurations, closed under singletons, subsets and finite unions (an 'antifilter', i.e. an ideal of subsets).

Page 10 then defines the set F of figures. A figure is a subset Φ ⊂ F_el which is (a) a configuration, (b) closed downward for ≤ (X ∈ Φ and X' ≤ X imply X' ∈ Φ), and (c) locally finite. Finite figures are finite subsets satisfying (a) and (b). The last condition (c) is added between the lines as '(localisation)'.

Grothendieck then records the relation that must link structures (2) and (3), first labelled 'Axiome' and then 'Fig_1': if X1, X2 ≤ X are elementary figures, then {X1, X2} is compatible, i.e. a configuration. Consequence: the principal down-set ↓X = {X' ≤ X} is a configuration and, being down-closed, a figure, called 'the figure associated to X'. This gives a map F_el → F, which is the way elementary figures embed into figures.

Page 11 continues with an axiom of finite combinatorial dimension (chains below X have bounded length) and defines combinatorial dimension. Purpose: to replace point-set topology with a poset-plus-compatibility calculus of figures, as in the 'géométrie modérée' programme of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The bracket justifies that ↓X is a figure 'en vertu de a) b)', but a figure also requires condition (c), local finiteness. This needs an extra argument, e.g. that the down-closure of a locally finite configuration (here a singleton) is locally finite, which page 9 axiom b) seems intended to supply. It is a minor gap, not an error.
The bracket says 'la figure associée à F'; it should read 'associée à X'.

ideas.what: Figures as down-closed, pairwise-compatible (and locally finite) subsets of a poset of elementary figures with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation
ideas.modern_name: Configurations of a prime event structure (down-closed consistent sets); ideals/cliques in a coherence space; subcomplexes of a face poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel 1981 (event structures, 'configurations'); Girard 1986-87 (coherence spaces); classical face-poset combinatorics
ideas.where_published: Tame-topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and Récoltes et Semailles, without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Axiom Fig_1: elements below a common element are compatible, so ↓X is a figure (the figure associated to an elementary figure)
ideas.modern_name: Consistency of principal ideals; consequence of conflict inheritance in event structures; faces of a simplex lie in a common simplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in event structures (Winskel) and simplicial complexes

ideas.what: Locally finite configurations forming an antifilter (ideal), used as a finiteness/localisation condition on figures
ideas.modern_name: Ideal of 'small' subsets, akin to local finiteness of CW/stratified complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics for tame topology is formally the structure of a prime event structure: events = elementary figures, causality = ≤, consistency = compatibility R (the complement of conflict), configurations = pairwise consistent sets, figures = down-closed configurations (Winskel's 'configurations'). Fig_1 is a consequence of Winskel's conflict-inheritance axiom, and the next page's finite combinatorial dimension echoes the finiteness-of-causes axiom. The same structure (reflexive symmetric relation, cliques) is Girard's coherence space of the same years. Even the word 'configuration' coincides. No literature seems to link Grothendieck's tame-topology foundations to event structures, domain theory or coherence spaces.
missed.quote: Si X_1, X_2 ≤ X sont des fig. él. alors {X_1, X_2} ∈ R i.e. {X_1, X_2} est une configuration. [Donc l'ens des X' ≤ X est une configuration, et en vertu de a) b) c'est même une figure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that the domain of figures of a tame space is a Scott domain / dI-domain (figures ordered by inclusion), opening a bridge between tame or o-minimal geometry and domain-theoretic or concurrency semantics. It also gives a precise lens for reading the rest of the manuscript.

missed.claim: A purely combinatorial axiomatization of tame spaces via (F_el, ≤, R, locally finite configurations) was started here but, as far as known, never completed or published. The later tame-topology literature (o-minimality) took a model-theoretic route instead.
missed.quote: On définit dans l'ens F des figures, comme l'ens des parties ... qui sont a) des configurations b) fermées par la relation d'ordre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an alternative, poset-based foundation for Grothendieck's 'géométrie modérée' that could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions and face posets of stratifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary (down-closed cliques in a poset with a compatibility relation). It is notable as an unpublished axiomatic start of Grothendieck's tame topology, and for its striking unremarked coincidence with event structures and coherence spaces of 1981-87.
transcription_corrections: 'E_el' is Grothendieck's script 'F_el' (set of elementary figures) throughout.
The 'Φ = Σ'_F' formula is unclear; it most plausibly denotes a subset Φ ⊂ F_el (the set of figures being called F, or 𝔉).
Interlinear insertion near b): '{+ c) (localisation)+}' adds a third condition (local finiteness) to the definition of figures; 'Figures finies' are then defined by a) and b) only.
The final bracket reads 'la figure associée à X' (not F).
'la relation entre (2) et (3)' refers to the order relation (2) and the compatibility relation (3) of page 9.
